##### The dimension-nine comparison

There are two dimension-sensitive steps in the proof.

exclusions.query: nonplanar monotone solutions in dimension nine or higher
exclusions.reason: Such solutions exist; the rigidity theorems stop at dimension eight.
Nonplanar stable solutions exist there, so the stable classification is sharp.

Let $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^8,(-1,1))$ satisfy $$\Delta u=u^3-u,\qquad \partial_8u>0\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^8.$$ Then there are $e\in\mathbb S^7$ with $e_8>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R$ such that $$u(x)=\tanh\!\left(\frac{e\cdot x-c}{\sqrt2}\right)
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^8.$$

Let $v\in C^2(\mathbb R^7,[-1,1])$ be a stable solution of $\Delta v=v^3-v$. Then either $v\equiv1$, $v\equiv-1$, or $$v(x)=\tanh\!\left(\frac{a\cdot x-b}{\sqrt2}\right)
 \qquad\text{for some }a\in\mathbb S^6,\ b\in\mathbb R.$$ No energy-growth assumption is required.

Let $4\le n\le7$. Suppose $v\in C^2(\mathbb R^n,[-1,1])$ solves $\Delta v=v^3-v$ and satisfies $$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\bigl(|\nabla\varphi|^2+(3v^2-1)\varphi^2\bigr)\,\mathrm dx
 \ge0
 \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^n).$$ If $M_\infty<\infty$, then $v\equiv1$, $v\equiv-1$, or $v(x)=g(a\cdot x-b)$ for some $a\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$ and $b\in\mathbb R$.

Let $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^8,(-1,1))$ solve $\Delta u=u^3-u$ and satisfy $u_8>0$. There are smooth stable solutions $v_-,v_+:\mathbb R^7\to[-1,1]$ such that $$u(x',t+s)\longrightarrow v_\pm(x')
 \quad\text{in }C^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^8)
 \quad\text{as }s\to\pm\infty,
 \qquad k\ge0.
 \label{eq:monotone-end-convergence}$$ They satisfy $v_-(x')<u(x',t)<v_+(x')$ everywhere. Their extensions independent of the eighth coordinate are global minimizers in $\mathbb R^8$.

Let $u:\mathbb R^N\to[-1,1]$ be an entire global minimizer with $\mathcal E(u;B_R)\le CR^{N-1}$ for $R\ge2$. Given $R_j\to\infty$, set $\varepsilon_j=R_j^{-1}$ and $u_j(x)=u(R_jx)$. After taking a subsequence there is a locally finite-perimeter set $E$ such that $$\begin{aligned}
 u_j&\longrightarrow 2\mathbf1_E-1
                    &&\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^N),\\
 \left(\frac{\varepsilon_j}2|\nabla u_j|^2+
                \frac{W(u_j)}{\varepsilon_j}\right)\,\mathrm dx
   &\rightharpoonup s_0|D\mathbf1_E|
                    &&\text{as local Radon measures}.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:monotone-exact-limit}$$ The set $E$ is locally perimeter minimizing against compact perturbations.

Let $E\subset\mathbb R^8$ be locally perimeter minimizing. Suppose its nonempty boundary support $C$ is a cone with vertex $0$ and $\partial_8\mathbf1_E\ge0$. Then $C$ is a hyperplane, with perimeter multiplicity one.

If Theorem 3 fails in a fixed dimension $4\le n\le7$, there is a nonplanar entire stable solution with finite integer density $M_\infty=K\ge2$, and a nonempty closed set $Z$, with the following properties. Put $s(x)=\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,Z)$ and $\Sigma=\{v=0\}$.* 1. *Uniformly for $y\in Z$, $$M_r(y)\longrightarrow K,\qquad r^{2-m}|B_1(Z)\cap B_r(y)|\longrightarrow0 \quad(r\to\infty).$$ The second conclusion holds with $B_h(Z)$ in place of $B_1(Z)$ for each fixed $h<\infty$.* 2. *There are $c>0,C<\infty$ and uniform moduli tending to zero as $s\to\infty$ such that, about each $z\in\Sigma$ with $s(z)$ large, the zero set in an interior cylinder of radius $c s(z)$ consists of exactly $K$ ordered smooth graphs. They are defined on a disk of that radius over a hyperplane through $z$, their heights are $o(s(z))$, their slopes are $o(1)$, and $$\|\nabla^2 f_i\|_\infty+ s(z)^{1/2}[\nabla^2 f_i]_{C^{1/2}}\le C/s(z), \qquad |H_i|\le C_\iota s(z)^{-2+\iota}.$$ Their separations tend uniformly to infinity. At the inner zero points $D=o(1)$, and every fixed normal window converges smoothly to the oriented $g$-profile.* 3. *Uniformly for $y\in Z$, $$\label{eq:finite-discrepancy} r^{-m}\int_{B_r(y)}q^2D\longrightarrow0.$$* *Constants and moduli in this lemma may depend on the fixed critical solution and dimension.

On $\Sigma_S$, for $S$ sufficiently large, let $l(z)$ be the shortest Euclidean distance to a distinct sheet in the local good chart. This definition is independent of the chart. Uniformly as $s(z)\to\infty$, $$l(z)\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad l(z)=o(s(z)).$$ Locally $l$ is the minimum of the smooth distance functions to the one or two adjacent sheets. On an active branch $l_b$, with nearest foot $z'=\pi_b(z)$, one has $$\label{eq:B5}
 \Delta_\Sigma l_b
 \le |H(z)|+|H(z')|+\frac{C}{s(z)}|\nabla_\Sigma l_b|^2.$$ Every measurable choice of an active foot has inverse multiplicity at most two. The branch area Jacobian is $1+o_S(1)$, and $$s(z')/s(z)=1+o_S(1),\qquad
 |z'-y|/|z-y|=1+o_S(1)\quad(y\in Z).$$

There is $C<\infty$ such that, at all sufficiently distant good zeros, $$\label{eq:B8}
 l(z)\le C\bigl((\log s(z))^2+s(z)^{1/10}\bigr).$$

Fix $4\le n\le7$ and $0<K_f<\infty$. There are $c>0,C<\infty,r_0<\infty$, depending only on $n,K_f$, such that every entire stable parameter-one solution with $M_r(z)\le K_f$, $r\ge r_0$, satisfies $$|

 \quad\hbox{on }B_{cr}(z)\cap\{|v|\le0.9\}.$$ For each prescribed slope tolerance and each fixed $\iota>0$, if $v(z)=0$, a sufficiently thin slab confinement of the zero set in this ball about a hyperplane through $z$ gives, on a smaller cylinder, ordered graphs with that slope tolerance and $$\|

The function $d$ is finite and positive on $\Sigma_{\rm reg}$. At every such point, writing $\lambda_i$ for the eigenvalues of $A$, $$\label{eq:reach-elementary}
 d\max_i|\lambda_i|\le2,
 \qquad |(y-z)\cdot\nu(z)|\le C_\Gamma |y-z|^2/d(z)
 \quad(y\in\Sigma).$$ For each $J<\infty$ there is a uniform $\delta(J)>0$ such that $v(z)=0$ and $D(z)<\delta(J)$ imply $d(z)>J$. Moreover, at every regular base there are zero-free open balls tangent at that base on both normal sides, of radius $c_\Gamma d(z)$.

There are fixed $C,c>0$ and a fixed density bound $K_0<\infty$ such that, if $d=d(z)$ is sufficiently large, then $$\label{eq:C1}
 h=d\exp\{-C\sqrt{\log(K(d)+1)}\},\qquad M_h(z)\le K_0.$$ The constant $C$ can be increased without invalidating the conclusion. In particular $h\ge d^{1-o(1)}$, uniformly as $d\to\infty$.

For sufficiently large $d(z)$, $D(z)+a(z)\le C_\Gamma/d(z)$. If $X=\{z\in\Sigma:D(z)\ge\delta\}$ with fixed $\delta>0$, then for every fixed $L_0$ there is a finite uniform upper bound for $d(z)$ at all good zeros with $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(z,X)\le10L_0$. The same conclusion holds for a contact reach $d(z)$ when its second foot $y$ satisfies $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(y,X)\le10L_0$.

For each $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $P_\varepsilon<\infty$ and, for each fixed $P\ge P_\varepsilon$, a number $\delta_{\varepsilon,P}>0$ such that every zero with $0<D(z)<\delta_{\varepsilon,P}$ is regular and satisfies $$\label{eq:L1}
 cD(z)\le I_P(z)\le C_P D(z),\qquad
 I_P(z)\ge(1-\varepsilon)|A(z)|^2,\qquad
 |H(z)|\le\left(\frac1{2\sqrt2}+\varepsilon\right)I_P(z).$$ The constants and thresholds are independent of the solution and center. The constant $c>0$ can be chosen independently of $P\ge1$.

There exist $\lambda>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending on the fixed penalty and dimension but independent of $\delta\in(0,1/4]$, such that $$\label{eq:L5}
 D(z)\le C\bigl(J_0(z)+E(z)\bigr),\qquad
 E(z)\le C\bigl(J_0(z)+D(z)\bigr),\qquad z\in\Sigma\setminus X,
 \quad J_0(z)=\sup_{y\in\Sigma}e^{-\lambda|y-z|}\bar a(y)^2.$$

Let $p_0>n$, $V_g=3g^2-1$, and $L_g=-\Delta_y-\partial_t^2+V_g(t)$ on $\mathbb R^m\times(0,\infty)$, with zero Dirichlet trace. For some $b_0>0$, uniformly in $0\le b\le b_0$, its inverse maps the norm $$\sup_{(y,t)}e^{-b|y|}\|f\|_{L^{p_0}(B_1(y,t)\cap\{t>0\})}$$ to the analogous uniformly local $W^{2,p_0}$ norm. The inverse is unique in this weighted class.

For $0<\delta\le1/4$, the area of $\Sigma\setminus X$ in any unit ball is bounded by a dimensional constant, independently of $\delta$. Consequently its area in an ambient ball of radius $r\ge1$ is at most $C(1+r)^n$. At a good zero whose distance from $X$ exceeds $2$, there is a fixed-size graph neighborhood on which $D$ is comparable to its value at that zero and $|\nabla_\Sigma A|\le C\sqrt D$.

Fix $\omega>0$, $C_0<\infty$, and a fractional margin $0<\theta_0<1$. Suppose that $z_0\in\Sigma$ and $$D(w)\le N^{-\omega}\qquad
 (w\in\Sigma\cap B_{N^\omega}(z_0)),\qquad N\longrightarrow\infty.$$ The following conclusions hold uniformly for bases $z\in\Sigma\cap B_{(1-\theta_0)N^\omega}(z_0)$. Local zero pieces within $C_0\log N$ of $z$ are finitely many ordered smooth graphs over $T_z\Sigma$. Their domains contain a disk of radius $cN^{\omega/8}$, with a further comparable graph buffer. They have curvature at most $CN^{-\omega/2}$ and slopes and differences of unoriented normals at most $$C\bigl(N^{-\omega/8}\log N+N^{-3\omega/8}\bigr).$$ Distinct graphs have Euclidean separation at least $c_0\log N$ where they participate in these neighborhoods.*

*For every fixed $k>0$, these descriptions extend over lateral disks of radius $(\log N)^k$ and through every fixed multiple of $\log N$ in normal depth. They contain every zero piece meeting the corresponding smaller cylinder. Projection to each participating local graph is unique and smooth there. Differences between its Euclidean distance and its vertical distance, and differences between its height increments and those of its tangent plane, are additive errors bounded by $$C_kN^{-c}(1+\log N)^{C_k}=o(1),\qquad c=c(\omega)>0.$$ The same bounds hold uniformly as the center moves in the stated fractional interior. In particular the lateral domains include $(\log N)^2$ boxes and disks of radius $\ell^{2/3}$ whenever $\ell=O(\log N)$. The polynomial buffers and unique projections make these descriptions consistent on overlaps.*

*If a distinct graph is within $C_0\log N$ of the base $z$, then $$d(z)=G_1\ell_{\min}(z),$$ where $\ell_{\min}(z)$ is the shortest Euclidean distance from $z$ to an adjacent graph. All thresholds may depend on the fixed parameters and on $k$, but not on the solution or the base.

In the seven-dimensional stable setting above, fix the penalty $\Gamma$ sufficiently close to the choices specified in Section 1, with $\eta_0<10^{-4}$ and $G_1-1,(1-\delta_2)^{-1}-1<10^{-3}$, decreasing these errors if required by Section 1. There are a finite $P$, a positive $\delta$, and constants $R_0,C<\infty$ such that, for every solution in the setting above, every $x_c\in\mathbb R^7$, every maximal net $\mathcal X$, and every $R\ge R_0$, $$\label{eq:M1} \mathcal Y_R:= \int_{\Sigma_g}\chi^2(a^4+D^2+E^2)+N_R \le C K(R)R^{m-4}.$$ The constants depend on the fixed penalty and tolerances, including $\delta$, but are independent of the solution, the center, the net, and $R$. Any prescribed smaller positive tolerances in [eq:L1]–[eq:L4] and [eq:L12]–[eq:L13] may be imposed before $P$ and $\delta$ are fixed.

For each $\varepsilon_2>0$ there are choices of the interface tolerances and $\delta>0$ such that, uniformly for all centers and sufficiently large $R$, $$\label{eq:M2}
 A_4:=\int_{\Sigma_g}\chi^2a^4
 \le\varepsilon_2\int_{\Sigma_g}\chi^2D^2
       +C_{\varepsilon_2,\delta}N_R
       +C_{\varepsilon_2,\delta}K(R)R^{m-4}.$$ The constants remain valid on decreasing $\delta$ once the preceding interface tolerances have been fixed, except for the displayed allowed dependence of the last two coefficients on $\delta$.

Let $\zeta_0=.01$ and $k=1.53$. Increase $t_{\min}$, before fixing $\delta$, so that $\exp(C/(\gamma t_{\min}^{\gamma}))<1.001$, where $C,\gamma$ dominate the errors in [eq:C8]. For every finite $t_*\ge t_{\min}$, every $\varepsilon_3>0$, and every $\eta>0$, there are $t_0>t_*$ and a function $f$ as in Lemma 40 such that, with $$B_*(t)=1+Ct^{-\gamma}+\zeta_0\mathbf1_{\{t\ge t_0\}},\quad p_*(t)=\exp\int_{t_{\min}}^t\frac{B_*(s)}s\,\,\mathrm ds,\quad P_*(t)=\frac1{p_*(t)}\int_t^\infty p_*(s)f'(s)^2\,\,\mathrm ds,$$ one has $-P_*'=f'^2+B_*P_*/t$ almost everywhere and $$\label{eq:M6} \begin{gathered} tP_*(t)\le .79f(t)^2\qquad(t_{\min}\le t

Uniformly for $\tau\ge\log R$ and $t\ge t_{\min}$, where $t_{\min}>0$ is any fixed lower bound for the reach on the good set, $$\label{eq:R1}
\begin{split}
 \mathcal F_\tau
 &=(1+o_R(1))\,cW_*
       \left(\frac{t}{c\tau\vee b(t)}\right)^\vartheta,\\
 \frac{\mathcal F_\tau+\mathcal F}{W_*}&\le C(L+\tau),\qquad
 \frac{\mathcal F}{W_*}\ge\frac1{q_*+\vartheta/t_{\min}},\\
 \mathcal F&\le C(L+\tau)^{1-\vartheta}.
\end{split}$$ On the regular zero surface the following is a distributional measure inequality: $$\label{eq:R2}
\begin{split}
 \Delta_\Sigma\mathcal F\ge{}&
 \mathcal F_\tau\Delta_\Sigma\tau
 -c^2\vartheta J_1|\nabla_\Sigma\tau|^2
 -W_*(\Delta_\Sigma d)_{\rm upper}\\
 &+\frac{\vartheta W_*}{d}|\nabla_\Sigma d|^2
 +\frac{W_*\lambda}{b'}|\nabla_\Sigma(c\tau-b(d))|^2,\\
 J_1={}&\int_{b(d)}^\infty
 u^{-\vartheta-1}f_*'(c\tau-u)\,\mathrm du
 \le C\mathcal F_\tau/\tau.
\end{split}$$ The last square is defined to be zero where $b'=0$.

Fix $C_0<\infty$. For all sufficiently large $R$, the common graph and projection conclusions of Lemma 36 apply within distance $C_0\log\rho(z)$ of every zero satisfying $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(z,Z)>\rho(z)^{\beta_0}/3$. They apply in particular at every base with $m_H\ne0$, uniformly for $\rho\ge R$ and independently of $B$. The polynomial graph buffers accommodate every fixed logarithmic-power lateral disk. Besides the exact identity $d(z)=G_1\ell(z)$ whenever a distinct sheet is at logarithmic distance, where $\ell(z)$ is the shortest adjacent Euclidean gap, the following conclusions hold.* 1. *Two sheet distances within a fixed bounded amount of the least distance can compete only across an adjacent gap, on opposite sides of the point. Three sheets cannot so compete.* 2. *Fix a base $z_i$ and one normal side. Its only possible partner in a middle band is the first adjacent graph on that side. Write $\ell_{ij}$ for the distance from the fixed base to that graph, and suppose $\ell_{ij}\le C_0\log\rho$. Before the ray reaches that graph, at logarithmic depths in the stated window, its two sheet distances $s_i,s_j$ satisfy $$s_i+s_j=\ell_{ij}+o_R(1),\qquad \frac{\,\mathrm d}{\,\mathrm ds_i}\frac{s_i-s_j}{2}=1+o_R(1).$$ The ray traverses a fixed-width middle band at most once. The partner graph and $\ell_{ij}$ are fixed although the projected receiving point can move on that graph.* *All distance errors are additive and uniformly vanish. Buffered graph families and their projections agree on overlaps.
For all sufficiently large $R$, the set $$\{z\in\Sigma\cap B_{2R}:m_H(z)=1,\ d(z)\le L/2\}$$ has area at least $c K(R)R^m$, with $c>0$ independent of $R$ and of the selected center.
